description: EVI-EnSitePy (Electric Vehicle Infrastructure - Energy Estimation and Site Optimization Python tool) is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) Python package for designing, modelling and analysing EV charging sites; it replaces the earlier EVI-EnSite. Contents: it simulates the arrival and charging of light-, medium- and heavy-duty EVs at a hub under different station configurations (power rating, port count, charger efficiency, power modules, connector type, from Level 1 and 2 to DC fast charging), with photovoltaic and storage assets and custom loads on site. Modules cover charging control, energy management, steady-state DC microgrid power flow with resistive losses, temperature-dependent battery charge acceptance, trip and route planning, multi-site simulation and site optimisation, and outputs include power demand profiles and customer queue lengths and wait times. The page says it handles large sites of more than 100 ports. Producer: NLR Transportation and Mobility Research, part of EVI-X. Coverage: generic sites, US focus. Format and access: Python package; the page gives no public download link. Licence: not stated on the NLR page. Caveats: results depend on assumed vehicle schedules; availability outside NLR partnerships is not stated. Simulation uses: sizing charging hubs and their grid connection, testing energy management and behind-the-meter storage, and queue-based service planning. Related records: platform-nlr-evi-x-ev-charging-infrastructure-modelling-suite and data-nlr-heavy-duty-depot-charging-load-profiles.
